chunks: And from him, he raised it (mursal), from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Ya'qub ibn Ja'far, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) that he said:

I do not say that He is standing, so I would remove Him from His place; nor do I delimit Him to a place that He would be in; nor do I delimit Him to move in something from elements and body parts; nor do I delimit Him by the utterance of splitting a mouth.

But rather, just as God (Blessed and Exalted) said: "Be!" and it becomes — by His will, without any hesitation within Himself. He is Samad, Singular, not needing an associate to remind Him of His kingdom nor to open for Him the doors of His knowledge.

key_terms.أَحُدُّ: Delimiting or attributing limits — used here in the negative to assert divine transcendence
key_terms.تَرَدُّد: Hesitation or deliberation — negated here to affirm God's immediate, unwavering will
key_terms.صَمَد: Al-Samad — the Self-sufficient, the Eternal, the Independent (a divine name from Quran 112:2)
key_terms.فَرْد: Al-Fard — the Singular, the Unique, the One without equal
key_terms.كُنْ فَيَكُونُ: The divine creative command 'Be! And it becomes' — cited from Quran 36:82
key_terms.مَشِيئَة: Divine Will — the absolute and immediate creative power of God

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Kazim say about God's transcendence of physical attributes?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) explains how God transcends all physical attributes and limitations. He refutes four specific anthropomorphic conceptions of God: that God has a fixed standing position, that God is confined to a location, that God moves through physical body parts, and that God speaks through physical sound. He then affirms the divine creative command 'Kun!' (Be!) as the pure expression of God's self-sufficient will — without delay, partnership, or any need for assistance.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Yaqoub Bin Ja’far, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘I<sup>asws</sup> am not saying that He<sup>azwj</sup> is Standing, So I<sup>asws</sup> decline Him<sup>azwj</sup> from His<sup>azwj</sup> place, nor am I<sup>asws</sup> limiting Him<sup>azwj</sup> by a place for Him<sup>azwj</sup> to be in, nor am I<sup>asws</sup> limiting Him<sup>azwj</sup> that He<sup>azwj</sup> moves into something from the elements and the body parts, nor am I limiting Him<sup>azwj</sup> by words piercing a mouth,

but just as Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Says: “Be!”, so it comes into being by His<sup>azwj</sup> Desire, from without a hesitation from Himself<sup>azwj</sup>. He<sup>azwj</sup> is Samad, Individual, not needy to an associate to mention His<sup>azwj</sup> Kingdom to Him<sup>azwj</sup> not to open for Him<sup>azwj</sup> the doors of His<sup>azwj</sup> Knowledge’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (the narrator of the above Hadith), in a marfu‘ manner, from al-Hassan ibn Rashid from Ya‘qub ibn Ja‘far from abu Ibrahim (a.s.) who has said the following.

“I do not say that he is standing so I would remove Him from His place. I do not limit Him in a place. I do not limit Him by His moving in something with key elements of the body or body parts. I do not limit Him by ascribing the movements of mouth or tongue.

The truth is what Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, has said, Be and it comes into existence through His will without any planning in a soul. He is Self-sufficient and all alone. He does not need any partner who would speak of His kingdom or open the doors of His knowledge.”
